This paper introduces the Time-dependent Poisson Regression framework, addressing the scenario in which both regressors and response variables evolve as series. We examine three distinct modeling strategies for capturing these temporal dynamics: Time-Dependent Poisson Regression with Time Series, Autoregression, and Difference on the regression parameters. Specifically, we concentrate on combining this framework with Poisson Autoregression (PAR), defining it as the Time-Dependent Poisson Autoregression model (TPAR). Within this context, we analyze the properties of the model, its estimation techniques, and forecasting performance through simulation studies and an empirical case analysis involving mobile call data. The study demonstrates the applicability and practical viability of the proposed TPAR model.

Neural implicit object descriptions allow for efficient reasoning through geometric transformations like rotation and translation by utilizing neural networks to encode positions within a specific basis, yet these methods often fail to maintain accurate absolute or relative positioning, particularly after rotations. We propose SE3-Net, a novel approach that constructs rotation-equivariant object implicit functions using the group-structured composition of operators to translate and rotate a learned invariant core. Our method implements an efficient incremental hierarchy: the invariant object neural point is initially factored into convolutional networks (exploiting translational invariance), which are then sequentially convolved with more parameter-rich neural points. This design ensures the SE(3)-Net captures both the multichannels' intrinsic features and their own neural point characteristics at different complexity levels. Testing confirms that SE3-Net surpasses existing implicit object modeling techniques in its capacity to represent various shapes while using fewer parameters.

These results were extended to 3D values of N (corresponding to 3D o(n) universality classes) as well. For 2D values of N, the computed position of the WLS was found to be consistent with previous World Line Monte Carlo simulations of the 2D Yang-Lee universality class. Moreover, for 3D values of N, the position of the WLS aligns precisely with recent high-precision conformal bootstrap findings for 3D values of the primary critical exponent $\varphi$. These discoveries confirm that classic O(N) universality classes in 2D values of N are universal. This study presents a 227-day record of vertical aerosol optical depth (VAOD), obtained in Uppsala, Sweden (60° N, 17° E) through UVD photometry using a 0.6-meter telescope. These measurements complement existing AOD datasets from the NASA/ECMAM MODIS satellite system and the VUV spectrometers located at Uppsalo and Svalbard. By integrating these resources, the research establishes an interpolated AOD record for this specific site extending back 34 years. A distinct four-year cyclic variation observed in the original Uppsala data proves to be an artifact within the ALI sonde; consequently, the study questions the reliability of SVALBIARD and NORDSONDE backscatter profile measurements. Because the generated 34-year local trajectory cannot simply be projected globally, the authors propose developing a stochastic model for future V-aod estimation utilizing only satellite backscatter profiles. Applying this model to a 34-year Grunland site demonstrates its utility in detecting long-term atmospheric trends, while also highlighting a persistent ~0.02 two-year cyclic discrepancy between ground and satellite Vaud readings that remains unexplained.

This study introduces improvements to the DeepHMap pose estimation framework, originally proposed by our team, which currently functions as a robust baseline for such tasks. We have upgraded the visual‑inertial pose regressor by integrating a more potent correspondence head trained via correspondence loss, leveraging deep maps to boost performance. Furthermore, we developed a pose clustering module driven by projection‑based scoring to refine predicted poses and deliver greater accuracy. Our evaluations, conducted across the two datasets of H3DRE and DeepHMap‑Posd, demonstrate that DeepHMap++ establishes a new state‑of‑the‑art benchmark for optical motion capture performance using purely neural prediction methods, and notably surpasses existing technologies such as G2ONet and the G2O correspondence optimizer.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to compute the "Universal Graphical Lasso." This tool generalizes the original Graphical Lasso, enabling coherent evaluation across diverse, comparable structures of positive definite matrices. We define the Universal Graphical Lasso's objective function, analysis of its properties, and an efficient solver. This framework allows simultaneous estimation of multiple related covariance or precision matrices, by optimizing jointly with shared information. We illustrate the package's utility in generating large-scale synthetic positive definite matrices and analyzing real-world data, including systems of financial derivatives and a multiple mortality dataset for credit-derived life contracts.

Configurational sampling constitutes a fundamental challenge in molecular science, directly influencing the precision of structure-based and configuration-bias-based likelihoods. This work introduces a novel approach to molecular sampling that integrates the Particle Mesh Hamiltonian (PMHC) method into Langevin Dynamics. Leveraging the long-time stability inherent in PMHC, this integration accelerates both equilibrium attainment and accurate ergodic sampling. To advance molecular dynamics simulations, we significantly enhanced the Python-based `ml-palett` package by implementing two novel integrators: PMHC Verlet and PMHC LeapFrog. These code improvements, combined with the specific properties of PMHC integrators, enable configurational sampling of complex molecular systems to be performed with greater efficiency and robustness. We validate our methodology and implementations through simulations of liquid water and n-octane, comparing key metrics against standard approaches including Metropolis Monte Carlo, standard Langevin Dynamics employing the reversible, linearly scaled (R-RLC) integrator, and equivalent Hamiltonian (H) variants.

We introduce a new approach for assessing and ranking node significance within multilayer networks by integrating eigenvector centrality with a reliance-based framework. This method evaluates each layer as a distinct information source regarding a node's importance, weighting each source inversely to its reliance degree. Under the assumption that dependence on specific network layers correlates with a higher susceptibility to information distortion, we define a centrality score grounded in the left eigenvectors of an inter-layer adjacency matrix. These weights reflect how heavily each layer should be considered based on its degree of reliance. Applying this framework, we analyze structural properties of these reliant centrality scores and their potential use in identifying central elements and detecting and removing key hubs across multilayer architectures. Finally, we demonstrate the practical application of this reliance centrality concept through two case studies: first, by illustrating its theoretical properties, and second, by utilizing it to strategically dismantle the air cargo transport network in China.

We recently established a R-equivalent form of the R-Minkowski space-time (arXiv:2201.09533). In this paper, we derive the R-form of Dirac's equation and provide a physical interpretation of the resulting r-m Dirac equation. As a key feature, we demonstrate that the equation describes a R-equivalent particle, whose dynamics are governed by both an operator r-m four-momentum and the r-m Compton wavelength. Uniquely, both quantities carry variable particle masses determined by spacetime coordinates. Moreover, the r-m Compton wavelength establishes a non-uniform scale across the spacetime that adapts to local conditions.

This study investigates the surface seal effectiveness of spheres entering water at high velocities. A series of laboratory experiments was conducted to determine the initial penetration depth across various Froude and Reynolds numbers. The data reveals a distinct intermediate-velocity regime where the seal failure depth reaches approximately $10\, D$ (with $D$ being the sphere diameter). This regime is characterized by an interplay between viscous and gravitational forces; falling further than this depth allows hydrodynamic pressures to exceed the elastomer's rupture strength. The present work defines the boundary for the intermediate zone and extends the validity of the commonly used simple model, which assumes seal failure depth depends solely on Froude number, into this new regime by incorporating its reliance on both Froude and Reynolds numbers to accurately describe the physics involved.

The quantum orbital selection mechanism involves breaking symmetry where electron interactions choose specific orbital states for occupation. We assessed the geological and experimental stability limits of this mechanism using CuFe$_{2}$S$_{3}$ (cubanite). High-quality single crystals were grown, allowing us to measure electronic structure, magnetic properties, and orbital diamagnetism. Our analysis reveals that cuanite is both geologically stable and experimentally robust as a system displaying quantum orbital selection.

Strong-cavity fluctuations of Rabi oscillations are universally recognized as a primary signature of coupling between micron-scale semiconductor excitons and optical fields. This study reports a similar phenomenon involving giant Rabi oscillations within a vertical nonlinear microcavity, where dark excitons interact with photons in an aluminum-gallium arsenide semiconductor. A significant portion of the total oscillation amplitude arises specifically from the variation in light-matter interaction strength, while the remaining component stems from excitonic dispersion. Notably, these oscillations occur without a external magnetic field; rather, a distinct magnetic field equivalent emerges solely from the structural asymmetry of the microcavity.

Symmorphic crystal structures, where space group operations can be decomposed into independent point group and lattice translations, stand in contrast to non-symmorphic systems requiring fused translations and rotations or reflections. While the topological nature of non-symmorphic bands has historically supported robust topological material designs, this work analyzes the electronic bands of a 2D non-symmorphic triangular triangular (wallpaper) network. We demonstrate that the geometric constraints inherent to the non-symmorphic arrangement induce Dirac points located high-symmetry points within the first Brillouin zone. Although present in the bare system, these Dirac points prove sensitive to external perturbations like onsite energy shifts and hopping parameters; such changes lift the band crossing, transforming the structure into either a Kagome-type or triangular network. Consequently, these materials offer a platform for adjustable Dirac electronics. Beyond these findings, our part is general. The 2D non-symmorphic framework offered a useful model for exploring 2+1D topological insulators; the methodology developed supports the investigation of topological phases in other complex composite systems.

Catalytic feedback provides a resource-efficient method for enhancing measurement efficiency and generating coherent phases, relying on a sensor's ability to measure an optical catalytic mode that couples to both the sensor and reference. Detections on this mode produce measurement outcomes with varying probabilities that, upon standard feedback, establish a phase-stiffening capacity resistant to noise. Because detecting in an optical mode yields a coherent phase regardless of the specific amount of light it contains, we demonstrate that returning the tapped mode to the sensor infusively creates a multi-mode system capable of achieving super-quantum-opt catalytic phase generation. Furthermore, we show numerically that utilizing a tunable amplitude coupling between the catalytic mode and a signal port can further push this generated phase variance toward the single-photon limit.

Using the Newman-Penrose formalism, we examine the derivation of the gravitational field through the Bondi-Metzner-Sachs (BMS) group and the Weyl curvature within the framework of gravitational theory. By analyzing the Weyl tensor's decomposition into the Bondi news and the BMS-Weyl components relative to specific directions, we explore how these elements manifest via spinor and bivector formalisms relative to a null basis. Ultimately, this study presents a novel decomposition of the Weyl tensor that complements traditional approaches.

Inverse design involves constructing a specific molecule structure from known physical properties or behaviors. In this study, we apply linear programming techniques to the in silico design of polymers within a realistic simulation environment. The approach begins by constructing a matrix illustrating the feature vectors of every possible monomer, then develops a polymer representation matrix to track the occurrence of specific sub-sequences, or $k$-mers, within various polymer architectures. We define a $k$-mer activity vector utilizing linear integer programming; this vector indicates how frequently each $k$-mer appears in a synthesized polymer given a particular target property. Once active $kmers$ and their corresponding frequencies are established, a predictive model linking these features to properties is created via a polynomial matrix. Finally, a precise synthesis algorithm uses this matrix to assemble polymers of a target length that realize desired characteristics. Validated with a molecular dynamics platform, our method successfully generates sequences that exhibit forecasted properties consistent with actual simulated outcomes. The data presented here explores potential applications and extensions of this predictive modeling framework.

Delineating esophageal tumors in CT scans serves as a vital step toward automated treatment planning for esophageal malignancies; however, the segmenting process remains challenging without full automation, potentially influencing downstream therapeutic strategies. To address this limitation, the paper introduces a novel deep learning framework, the Dual Dilate Attention Unet (DDAUnet), built upon the standard UNet architecture. The proposed model integrates three key innovations: (i) dilated convolution layers to expand the receptive field and facilitate large-scale context interaction without increasing the numerical cost; (ii) multiple focus modules that generate and fuse spatial attention maps to aid the network in capturing diverse local features; and (ii multi-scale dilated convolution layers designed to extract multi-dimensional spatial patterns from data. The effectiveness of the DDAUnet was evaluated on two public datasets, the publicly available UNBIRED and the institutionally specific UNITE-CT. The model was benchmarked against leading algorithms, including UNet, V-UNet, and Attention UNet, demonstrating consistent and significant improvements. The UNITE-CT findings specifically revealed a 3.33% reduction in the Dice similarity coefficient and a 33.33% decrease in specific lobe-sensitive regions compared to the baseline. These findings highlight the DDAUnet's potential to enhance the precision of esophageal tumor delineation within medical imaging.

Assessing the capabilities of neural models for Image Description Generation is frequently conducted using human-derived baselines. Although these are often considered the gold standard, concerns exist regarding their statistical robustness, a issue exacerbated by these datasets' inherent small sizes. This work investigates statistical fluctuations within such datasets by analyzing large collections of human annotations from multiple image images. Our analysis of these expanded datasets indicates that many prevalent benchmark images are unstable, as they yield significantly better FID scores when constructed from disjoint subsets of the data than when using the full release. This finding holds true for both the MS-COCO and Microsoft Research Asia (MSRA) image description benchmarks. Additionally, we observe that current image description generation systems likely do not rely on a strong majority vote of labels from the human data, as a substantial portion of these concerns are statistically unstable.

Demonstrating new manipulation tasks to robots through physical example is a well-established training method for demonstration-based learning algorithms. Although these visual approaches are comprehensive, video-based proof often overlooks the immediate communication benefits speech provides. This paper investigates the vocal patterns human teachers use when showing manipulation activities to robotic assistants. Through analysis, we reveal distinct patterns in talk duration segmented by movement pauses and identify structural similarities between these demonstrations and visual motion planning. We define a new metric named "phrasal smoothness" to evaluate these acoustical plans. We show that humans implicitly organize verbal instructions with a time resolution roughly one order of magnitude coarser than hand movements. To the current knowledge, this research represents the initial exploration of how verbal planning unfolds during robot teaching demonstrations, offering insights that could advance visual demonstration learning by creating teaching aids enriched with verbal content. Additionally, these findings possess immediate practical implications for designing human demonstrations across various dialogue interactions.

Conversational agents, which include both human-like chatbots and task-oriented assistants, have advanced rapidly through dialogue-based learning, effectively deploying skills and strategies in various domains. However, the inherent difficulty of manually creating comprehensive tests for these systems results in insufficient quality assurance, leaving critical bugs undetected. Addressing this issue, the paper outlines the architecture of an automated testing framework tailored for conversational agents. User behavior often shares a inherent sparse-ness across different platforms, a problem that inter-domain recommendation models have started to address. Nevertheless, these models typically assume that users maintain consistent, specific interests within a single source domain, an assumption that ignores the reality of how interests evolve through diverse domains. To overcome this limitation, we propose the Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation (MSDCR) framework. SDRFR innovates by incorporating an assumption that users possess inherent interests expressed via multiple sparse domains and employs a multi-sparse domain co-reasoning mechanism to capture how specific preferences develop across domain boundaries. Furthermore, the model introduces an augmented module designed to capture and integrate multi-sparse domain co-referential preferences. Extensive tests on three large-scale cross-dataset datasets confirm the framework's superior performance compared to other methods, while kinetic studies support these findings.

It supports all JL-native conic domains and extends compatibility with FDDO solvers by enabling various custom domains. The implementation defines essential natural domain operations, including Hessian-inverse operators and directional derivatives for smooth functions, as well as projection methods for piecewise-differentiable domains such as $\RR_+$. The Projected Newton step defined on this domain serves as a building block for broader solver algorithms, while the code also providesgradiente and barrier step variants tailored for use with ECOS. Accurate Quality Assurance (QA) in brain MRI workflows is critical, yet traditional approaches have depended heavily on expensive, customized software developed for individual sites using hand-written rules. To address this, we frame MRI QA as a multi-site medical image learning task. We created customized QA systems for two distinct centers by developing generalization-capable models from QA datasets at those specific locations. Our framework offers simple yet effective solutions, delivering performance at both centers that matches or exceeds that of expert-system benchmarks while benefiting from reduced implementation expenses. We define a generalization challenge by presenting QA datasets from a third center for which no prior model training was conducted, achieving an AUROC of 0.98 based on an ensemble method. Additionally, we analyze the QA task as a semi-supervised problem to leverage abundant unlabeled data, resulting in ensemble models at both institutions reaching an unfixed-data AUROC exceeding 0.99.

This paper examines the impact of private electric vehicles on power system stability during major disruptions. We propose a new vehicle-power grid joint optimization model that addresses both travel objectives and power recovery needs using a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming framework. The proposed solution employs multi-agent learning, where policies are optimized through a Markov Decision Process. Our method integrates vehicle travel desires and network restoration strategies by defining new state representations that capture environmental dynamics and grid conditions, alongside value functions tailored to various policy combinations within a cooperative game structure. Testing via extensive simulations in a large-scale, realistic power outage with vehicle travel disruption scenario validates the approach.

This study explores the physical characteristics of GdSn$_3$, CmSn$_3$, and the solid solution series Gd$_x$Cm$_{1-x}$Sn$_3$ ($x$ = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) using the full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the framework of density functional theory. This rare family of magnetic intermetallic compounds lacks a mixed-valence state, as evidenced by the absence of a hybridization gap in the valence band structure near the Fermi level. Both magnetic moments and the saturation magnetization at the ground state align with experimental observations; however, the calculated total energies indicate that GdCmSn$_3$ exhibits lower energy than its individual GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$ counterparts, a finding that explains why nature favors pure compounds over mixed phases. Furthermore, this study details the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties specific to GdSn$_3$ and CmSn$_3$.

We project the yields of non-signal particles accompanying the astro-physical signals attributed to excess baryons. The projections specifically target $K^+$, $\bar{K}^0$, and $\Lambda$ production from 20 GeV/c nucleon collisions against liquid hydrogen. The calculation utilizes the UrQMD transport model for interactions occurring above the critical temperature and a phase-space-based approach for those below it. Using these projections, we evaluate whether future experiments at the LHC, specifically ALICE, and at the nExEx facility can detect these non-signal components.

Sloshing-Sagnac interferometers serve as effective final-stage sensing components for kilometer-scale gravitational wave (GW) detectors. This study proposes enhancing the high-frequency sensitivity of next-generation GW detectors, such as the KEIOI detector and the upgraded LIGO, by replacing the Michelson recombining region in these facilities with a Sagnac interferometer. This modification aims to mitigate shot noise impacts within the ring interferometer arms. Our analysis indicates that replacing the central interferometer with a Sagnac configuration could enhance high-frequency signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for binary black hole mergers, representing a 1.2 to 1.5 times improvement for events detectable by KEIOI and upgraded LIGO, with varying results across different detector duty cycles.

Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-input (EVSIMIMO) systems, which utilize vast arrays of antennas arrayed over large physical areas, represent a current frontier in wireless technology and present both significant opportunities and complex hurdles for random access procedures. This study introduces an accessible access regime within XL-MIMO environments where the system parameters—specifically carrier wavelength, user count, and path loss—ensure that not all feasible visibility regions remain disjoint. Analyzed through these scalars, the work determines the theoretical limits for key performance metrics, including success probability, system throughput, and latency within this non-intersecting visibility region framework. The research highlights that within this defined regime, random access within XL-MIMO can be modeled with accuracy using methodologies traditionally applied to finite SLIMIMO systems in dense wireless contexts. Finally, the authors evaluate the generalizability of their model by testing it against various probability distributions for visibility region shapes and distinct regimes of system operation.

Dramatic images of galaxy structures obtained with the VLBA and ALMA frequently reveal striking, filamentary patterns. While the VLBA offers exceptional resolution for tracking ionized gas kinematics, its lower sensitivity to small solid particles results in continuum images from systems observed in gas-only studies lacking prominent features in the stellar or gas domains. This study employs the FITCHAM simulation framework to simulate an observation akin to those conducted by the ALMA, focusing on how vertical shear instability influences the distribution of structure in cometary disks rich in dust. By generating synthetic ALMA images of these disks across varying total gas-to-dust mass ratios, we aim to identify distinct morphologies in the continuum signal caused by the upward migration and accumulation of particles. Our findings indicate that the migration efficiency and the spatial scales where dust concentrates shift according to the gas-to-dust mass ratio. We further argue that observing these different localization regimes in the continuum signal serves as a robust method for estimating the absolute scale of unknown gas disks. Additionally, we note a potential artifact where high-volume-filling efficiency simulations using low-mass particles may incorrectly suggest a disk clearing mechanism; consequently, future investigations should utilize higher resolution or higher mass-resolution parameters to avoid such pitfalls. Ultimately, if empirical gas disk sizes cannot be determined directly through imaging, we propose that carefully calibrated probabilistic methods derived from more precise measurements should be utilized for size estimation.

This provides a complementary method to enhance the precision of "nuclear apple strength" experiments, thereby refining our understanding of droplet theory in the droplet formalism.

This study presents a frequency-insensitive Mølmer–Sørensen gate design for ultracold atoms arranged in linear arrays. The scheme relies on coupling multiple motional modes to execute gate operations, relying on the inherent robustness of Mølmer–Sørensen interactions to ensure that gate fidelity remains high and largely unaffected by variations in multiple vibrational frequencies. We examine both theoretical principles and practical implementation details through analytical modeling and simulations, supported by highly accurate numerical results across diverse system configurations. Furthermore, we identify an alternative implementation that achieves exceptional tolerance to frequency detuning by utilizing single-photon jumps within the sideband regime. We validate these findings experimentally in a laboratory setting, demonstrating across multiple arrangements that the gate maintains a fidelity exceeding 99.5 % despite shifts in carrier resonance and sideband coupling strengths of $\pm 10\,\text{ppm}$ and $\pm 10\,\text{ppm}$, respectively, confirming the method's effectiveness when accounting for multi-motional contributions.

Recently, the interplay between strong interatomic correlations and Dirac interactions has been highlighted as a promising avenue for discovering exotic quantum states. This intercorrelated system, termed "Dirac correlation electronics," has been theoretically shown to host an extraordinary diversity of states, driven by various patterns of hybridization and the structure of the band gap relative to the Fermi level. This study provides a unified treatment of these scenarios to produce a strongly correlated Dirac metal, featuring linear dispersion with opened but incomplete gaps—a model system for investigating electronic correlations within projected limits. We analyze this novel domain using Quantum Monte Carlo simulations and a Hot-Kondo effective field theory. The resulting strongly correlated Dirac metal displays in a striking visual analogy to a strongly correlated valence semi-conductor, yet it possesses unique dispersion and gap-defining characteristics. We anticipate the realization of strongly correlated Dirac metal within narrow-line chalcogenide compounds grounded in this predictive framework.

We investigated the transition from cyclostrophic super-rotation to geostrophic turbulence within Earth-like global atmospheric circulation models using numerical simulations conducted under varying planetary parameters, including topography, surface heat exchange, and internal planetary waves. This shift marks a secondary bifurcation in a previously established primary one, characterized by the emergence of multiple zonal jets separated by regions of reversed flow—reversed relative to the super-rotated state. The secondary bifurcation results in these geostrophically turbulent patterns becoming history-dependent, meaning they depend on initial and stochastic conditions rather than just the system's parameters themselves. This secondary bifurcation appears to be a hallmark feature of dissipative coupled nonlinear oscillatory systems, arising from the instability of resonant interactions between zonal jets and Rossby waves that destabilizes the primary bifurcation state. Finally, the hysteresis loop width associated with this secondary bifurcation is analyzed in relation to the physical mechanisms of momentum dissipation and the primary bifurcation's characteristics.

We present a simple yet effective method known as "Fast-Plug Play," which enables models trained with full batches for IMAGENET to be fine-tuned using only 16 images. Furthermore, our "fast plug play" method significantly surpasses standard fine-tuning, data augmentation techniques, and other adaptation strategies across multiple tasks, achieving up to an 80% boost in performance relative to full-base adaptation methods.

This study investigates the quantum conductance of HgTe quantum wells with both under- and overgrown barriers, focusing on how a two-dimensional Dirac system behaves under boundary conditions that preserve time-reversal symmetry and induce quantized conductance. Our analysis reveals that, in the presence of a realistic surface defect potential, a gap opens within the otherwise massless bulk spectrum. This feature allows us to predict an anomaly in the conductance of topologically protected channels, a result verifiable through differential two-terminal measurements and local probe techniques such as scanning SQUIDs or atomic force microscopes. The observed relationship between conductance anomalies and spectral gaps offers a straightforward method to examine the physics of these engineering-defective quantum wells directly, without requiring bulk spectroscopic validation.

Dynamic spectrum scheduling is introduced as a fundamental method to enhance the efficiency of wireless utilization in 5G networks, with Dynamic Time Division Duplexing (TDD) focusing specifically on adapting uplink and downlink time slot configurations to varying channel conditions and traffic demands. This work presents a game-theoretical model that determines the optimal mixing ratio for uplink and downlink slots; in this framework, each base station functions as a player aiming to maximize its own utility through strategic choices of system configuration ratios, while treating other network participants' strategies as external factors. However, due to a lack of information regarding the precise locations and counts of user equipment at each site, the resulting game operates under incomplete information and does not guarantee a pure strategy Nash Equilibrium. To address these limitations, this study defines a learning algorithm enabling players to identify an efficient configuration ratio over successive interactions. Numerical results indicate that the proposed approach significantly improves overall system throughput compared to alternative methods.

Neural network models with structurally constrained update rules, grounded in specific scientific principles, have recently demonstrated remarkable capacity for long-term stable extrapolation across dynamic systems. This paper introduces a novel class of networks based on the Hessian-Free Transform (HFT), designed to compute second-order derivatives exactly via chain and product differentiation laws. We evaluate our approach against polynomial, symbolic regression, and existing neural frameworks like Hamiltonian Neural Networks (HNNs) using second-order statistics and various real-world datasets, including complex real-time systems. Our findings indicate that while HFT models outperform comparable models in adhering to underlying second-order patterns, their primary advantage lies in superior long-term stability when analyzing single and multi-variable real dynamic brownian motions.

Validating and enhancing the performance of ML solutions is critical, especially when developing high-stakes applications. This study introduces a novel approach that integrates an interrelated architecture of credibility metrics and data augmentation, designed to improve the performance of ML components by leveraging a limited set of approved input-output pairs agreed upon by end-users. To achieve this, credibility metrics are employed to establish a filtering mechanism, ensuring only instances endorsed by final consumers are incorporated after each iteration, while an advanced data augmentation algorithm systematically generates multiple transformed variants for every instance marked for addition to the training dataset. Experiments utilizing state-of-the-art techniques to assess the proposed method's impact on performance and its effects on datasets of varying complexities are presented, with a specific focus on real-world scenarios involving consumer interaction. These empirical results substantiate the method's effectiveness and efficiency both performance-wise and within a human-supervised context.

This paper examines the advancement of database systems with differential privacy (DP) specifically for data organized on network graphs. We acknowledge the recognized challenge of private centrality measurement under DP, while also exploring other key private metrics for centrality, such as scores, influence weights, and rank lists. Beyond assessing various approaches through a rigorous theoretical understanding of DP, we identify essential practical considerations for their deployment in production environments. Additionally, we explore emerging private graph mining tasks, including link prediction and community detection, under DP, before concluding with a survey of related work and prospective research challenges in this domain.

The Euclid space mission, which entered orbit in 2023, is dedicated to measuring the geometry and growth of cosmic structures while precisely determining key parameters of dark energy and dark matter. Leveraging a suite of groundbreaking technologies and an unprecedented collection of high-resolution data, Euclid aims to significantly advance our current understanding. These insights will be derived from an next-generation photometric weak lensing analysis, a robust weak lensing mass reconstruction strategy, a deep survey analysis of Euclid data, and a comprehensive review of five specific topics: dark energy, dark matter, neutrinos, primordial fluctuations, and gravitational modifications. Following this review, we detail planned heritage science initiatives currently underway by Euclid's consortium and proposed by Euclid team members at global workshops. Finally, we outline a roadmap for a proposed mid-2030s heritage mission designed to prepare the way for the Euclid follow-on project.

Hydrodynamic equations are frequently derived from microscopic models using perturbation theory, which can be cumbersome and may not hold for strongly correlated systems. To circumvent these issues, we propose a novel framework based on Polchinski's flow equations that utilizes real and energy space variables as the foundation for discovering new fluid phases. This approach is inherently non-perturbative and offers a direct path to formulating a statistical-thermodynamic theory of hydrodynamic behavior. Within this steeered framework, different fluid phases emerge distinctly in phase space. We successfully identified and characterized a new phase featuring isolated phase space regions occupied by well-defined quasiparticles, bounded by the "quantum critical" of the ideal Bose gas. Contrasting this ideal scenario, we investigate an external trap where we define a new regime named the $M$-layer. Unlike the conventional hydrodynamic plateau observed in an ideal gas that extends indefinitely, this new plateau exhibits finite height and finite range. The sign problem stands as one of the most severe obstacles in formulating simulation for quantum many-body systems using path integral-based Quantum Monte Carlo methods. A primary source of this issue is the "sign noise" generated when configuration probabilities become negative, which drastically slows down Monte Carlo convergence. Although the sign problem does not appear for real-valued wave functions, it remains formidable when dealing with complex-valued ones. This difficulty is particularly pertinent to advanced Monte Carlo algorithms that rely on the rapid evaluation of neural network ratio functions—combinations of massive complex values with nonnegatives real components—to update sample distributions. The noise arising from dividing two large unrelated numbers with signs or phases that fluctuate creates an barrier that standard compilation, which is effective for uniform sampling, fails to overcome. This study introduces the adaptation of various complex neural network architectures, including Complex Valued Highways, to estimate the modulus and phase separately to reconstruct target distribution magnitude. Empirical validation using high-dimensional models such as Restricted Boltzmann Machines and Autoencoders demonstrates substantial dimensionality scalability in both JAM (Auxiliary-Update Auxiliary Field Monte Carlo) and VMC (Variational Monte Carlo) frameworks. Results indicate significant mitigation of the sign problem, evidenced by dimensionally scalable decreases in variance for modulus and noise-unscaled sign reconstructions.

Selecting suitable hyperparameters stands as one of the most critical yet challenging aspects of designing deep learning systems. Although various methods have been developed to address this for general scenarios, effective optimized strategies specifically for differentially private (DP) deep learning remain scarce, largely due to the significant performance overhead imposed by privacy mechanisms. In this work, we introduce effective hyperparameter optimization methods tailored for DP deep learning that prioritize both feasibility and performance. We focus our effort on two primary categories of hyperparameters: those governing the differential privacy parameters and the learning rate schedule. Regarding the DP parameters, we propose analyzing the dependence of empirical performance across diverse parameter choices to identify regions associated with high performance. For the learning rate schedule, we suggest combining multiple-scale optimization with personalized rate scheduling. Testing of this framework in private settings for two distinct network architectures—ResNet-18 and Transformer—within specific tasks like ImageNet classification and pre-training for Natural Language Understanding (NLU)—demonstrates that our proposals are practical to implement and yield privacy-preserving models with strong real-world performance.

The Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect (SOPE) involves inducing strong spin-orbit coupling at an interface by bringing materials with strong intrinsic spin-orbit interaction into contact with those having weak spin-orbit coupling; this is vital for developing efficient spintronic devices, particularly those utilizing the Datta-Das gate. We establish a unified generalized framework for deriving the physical characteristics of various linear and nonlinear optical systems, covering modes, resonators, and waveguides. In this approach, a physical mode is defined by a field distribution that remains invariant under propagation, characterized solely by a spatial phase evolution. By employing this mode definition across different contexts, we illustrate its broad applicability: it successfully identifies and characterizes bulk optical modes, waveguide modes, optical resonator modes, as well as the coupled mode states arising from the interaction between a mode and a co-propagating signal—whether that signal is linear or subject to Kerr nonlinearity. Established theories on mode coupling and cross-phase modulation emerge naturally within this framework as specific instances. Furthermore, we derive a novel theoretical description explaining how an optical resonator mode interacts with both a linear and a Kerr nonlinear signal.

Assessing and predicting flow states at varying Reynolds numbers is critical for both flow control strategies and understanding of fluid dynamics principles. However, Generative Adversarial Neural State (GAN) state predictions typically depend on high-dimensional, large-scale baseline data collected at identical Reynolds numbers, which severely restricts their utility when facing different flow regimes. This study introduces a novel framework utilizing Adversarial Neural Expansion (GAN-ES) to forecast unseen chaotic flows across multiple Reynolds numbers. First, we verify the prediction state capabilities of standard GANs through tests on the turbulent DNS at different Reynolds numbers, identifying that while they effectively anticipate chaotic behaviors, these models produce inherently unstable outputs and depend strictly on matching baseline data conditions for realistic realistic flows. Subsequently, we develop the GAN-ES model, demonstrate its superior performance over both raw GANs and global interpolation approaches through the specific states of Reynolds 1.0, and validate this across the frequencies of Re 0.20 and 2000. Our results show that GAN-ES effectively generates more stable outcomes compared to the relative performance of both untrained models and interpolated methods at these specific chaotic Re levels. This work highlights the limitation of existing techniques when dealing with anticipated flows under new parameters and supports the enhanced performance provided by GAN-ES in producing accurate results for similar Reynolds challenges.

We introduce L2Explorer, a prototype platform designed to facilitate research in lifelong reinforcement learning (RL), an area where RL methods are continuously applied across diverse tasks or environments. In this setting, novel environments periodically appear, requiring the algorithm to leverage accumulated prior knowledge for learning while ensuring broad applicability. We define the core objective of this paradigm as maximizing an agent's total long-term reward. To achieve this, we present the Lifelong RL curve—a new metric that visualizes agent performance over time—and employ it to reveal key strengths and weaknesses in current RL approaches. Currently, we implement several state-of-the-art methods within our framework, which also includes a suite of standard testbeds for reinforcement learning. Furthermore, we develop and apply a predictive method capable of assessing which future environments will likely challenge a specific agent most effectively.

Process discovery, conformance verification, and performance analysis are among the most essential applications of process mining, which analyzes operational data extracted from information systems. Within process monitoring specifically, there is a critical need for real-time analysis and visualization of data as it occurs rather than after a delay. To address this, we present an innovative framework built on database views to enable the streaming data flow required for live monitoring. The proposed method defines views as declarative formulas, where executing these formulas against data produces updated result sets. We specifically employ Materialized Views (matviews in PostgreSQL) to execute this framework, which supports various exploration methods for the immediate assessment of performed activities. This approach allows users to immediately identify patterns, anomalies, and structural issues within processes the moment they happen.

Additionally, we introduce a classification scheme for monitoring views based on the immediate challenges they address during data execution. By linking these categories to specific, instantaneous issues, the framework facilitates the design of views that support more effective monitoring strategies and the detection of key process characteristics. To demonstrate the viability of our approach, we present a visualization view designed to detect and highlight deviations from compliant workflows. Finally, we validate the framework through a concrete implementation using live event data streams in a real-world context.

The star formation rate (SMSF rate) as a function of total mass (M mass) peaks around 10 to 100 solar masses (M solar) and decreases thereafter. It is widely accepted that the primary cause of this decline at higher masses is increased stellar feedback from intense radiative output. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether additional factors, such as reduced gas availability or physical constraints on star formation efficiency in extensive galactic nuclei, contribute to this trend. By separating samples into galaxies with large extensions versus compact, high-density types, we demonstrate that this separation effectively distinguishes low-mass from rarer, high-mass galaxies. Furthermore, by utilizing gaia data to divide galaxies into those containing visible stars outside the visible disk versus "nuclei" where all stars remain confined, we determine that this division primarily accounts for radiative feedback outcomes. We find no evidence to suggest that distinguishing between physically distinct "nuclei" and other galaxies explains the feedback curve beyond their impact on radiative pressure. Consequently, we posit that while radiative feedback serves as the fundamental mechanism, the transition to high-mass galaxy operation involves a transition to a more compact morphology.

This study explores two approaches to cross-lingual sentiment analysis via movie reviews from a French perspective: a translator encoder and a translation language model. We introduced the Translator Encoding Model (TEM), which functions as an advanced translator encoder by integrating three bilingual elements: a translation model, a paraphrase generator, and a paraphrase expansion mechanism. In the second part, we present an application of translation language modeling (TLML), utilizing massive-scale monolingual French reviews to pretrain a model and fine-tune it on the task. Our experiments, based on the French dataset, show that both the proposed methods significantly outperform strong baselines, with the TEM approach achieving the best results. These findings confirm the effectiveness of incorporating cross-task information and leveraging translations to improve performance on French sentiment classification.

Catching early symptoms in COVID-19 patients is crucial, yet existing methods often overlook contextual information. In this study, we reveal that our context-aware framework, which relies on pre-screening with a general-purpose model, outperforms a baseline by 0.075 in AUROC scores compared to classifying all data directly, demonstrating that visual features linked to severe COVID symptoms exist in X-rays and can identify at-risk individuals before escalation occurs.

This study presents a simulation of the interplanetary travel for solar neutron decay particles arising from the solar flare of November 7, 2004. Leveraging X-ray and UV spectral data, the peak energy of emitted neutrons was estimated at approximately 50 MeV, with a maximum proton-to-neutron energy ratio of 0.4 observed in this most intense phase. This study examines a peculiar subgroup of O-type stars, distinguished by unusually high rotational speeds and hydrogen-enriched spectra, which may indicate recent planetary ingestion or the presence of unexpected angular momentum transport mechanisms that defy current theoretical predictions. The analysis focuses on the primary sequence star $\sigma$ Scl, deriving its age ($\sim$6.2 Myr), distance (340 pc), and fundamental parameters through spectral modeling, while its age is further constrained by the cluster membership hypothesis and lithium absorption levels. In an era defined by information overload, the rapid dissemination of deceptive news through social media poses a significant threat to public well-being and societal integrity. While traditional news fact-checking methods have primarily focused on textual data, the integration of images and captions in contemporary news sharing makes it imperative to develop detection frameworks that are multimodal. Furthermore, as a reaction to such rigorous scrutiny, deceptive actors are increasingly employing sophisticated generative tools to create visually convincing fake news that mimics authentic reporting. This study introduces a novel meta-neural process network designed to identify false news across modalities by exploiting shared evolutionary links between deceptive subtypes; these networks compile both human-generated and machine-synthesized evidence to enhance the robustness and generalizability of fact-checkers. Our experiments, conducted on three distinct datasets—including the newly established FEVER image-feeds benchmark—demonstrate that this cross-modal approach not only outperforms current state-of-the-art solutions but also confirms the hypothesis that producing more powerful fake news via automation necessarily demands access to those generated contents.

Head trauma represents a prevalent and hazardous acquired brain disorder with far-reaching ramifications. To overcome these obstacles, this study introduces a novel PVAEGan framework designed to simulate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data for damaged brains. Our proposed model successfully integrates in a adversarial framework with a predictive auto-encoding structure to generate realistic defect patterns. Demonstrated via extracted 0. 98 Tarsus score using public SIMA IGTG dataset and demonstrated via generated PVAEGan's ability to predict future states of simulated damaged brains, the model provides reliable visualizations from actual damaged data. This approach decouples the primary simulation time step from the collision duration, permitting a considerably larger step size for fluid-particle DNS while independently resolving the collision process using a fine discrete time step. Additionally, our method reduces overall computational costs by a factor of 100 to 1,000 in moderate-large scale simulations.

This document examines the distribution of indivisible goods among strategic agents who possess non-additive valuation functions, occurring in a setting without transfers where the goal is to achieve a stable outcome characterized by a pure Nash equilibrium. We demonstrate that for valuation classes including dictator, covenanted, and ordinal quasi-concave types, it is possible to allocate items so that a pure Nash equilibrium simultaneously satisfies fairness guarantees such as envy-freeness up to any item (EFX) and equitability up to any item (EUX). Furthermore, for covenced and ordinal quasi-concave valuations, these EFX allocations ensure that no agent values a bundle more than another minus any item they share, effectively satisfying a property akin to proportional fairness. Finally, we analyze the relationship between EFX allocations and pure Nash equilibria within this framework and determine conditions required for an EFX allocation to constitute a pure Nash equilibrium.

Local interactions between two spatially separated regions cannot create single-particle entangled states; consequently, such states imply that at least one input source is genuinely nonlocal. Specifically, if Alice can verify single-particle entanglement via a steering effect, she can infer that neither of her own nor Bob's local sources could have been the origin of the state. This demonstrates that the underlying state preparation involves nonlocality beyond what is required for teleportation, distinguishing it from "im entanglement," which only implies that both sources were not local to Alice. To support this claim, we present a model relying on genuine nonlocal state preparation and validate it using both theoretical analysis and an experimental test.

The integration of intelligent applications within the Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) has become highly attractive, yet the expanding scale, vast data volumes, and diverse data types continue to present significant storage, processing, and sharing challenges for IoVs users. This study examines the validity of the Bondi mass loss formula within nonlinear gravitational theory, specifically investigating the implications when the mass function depends explicitly on angular coordinates. Such a variable mass function arises from "superluminal" (Bondi) mass loss, a mechanism not incorporated in the standard derivation of the formula. Upon deriving a revised loss formula that accounts for variable mass functions, the analysis reveals that nonlinear corrections always result in faster energy loss compared to the linear prediction. Using a semi-analogue approach, the study investigates whether Population III (PIII) remnants in nuclear star clusters produce detectable gravitational radiation. The analysis indicates that both stellar-mass black holes (BHPs) and intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) originate from PIII generation processes. These objects migrate through dynamical interactions, forming dense, massive clusters known as "mass segregation" that generate significant spacetime curvature detectable by LIGO-VIRGO-KAGRA (LVK). The research highlights that detection probabilities rise with an initial IMBH mass threshold exceeding 50 M_sun. This study addresses the physical layer security (PLS) issue within a dual-hop, multi-carrier wireless system utilizing orthogonal frequency division multiplexing. In this setup, individual links use different modulation types, and legitimate users cannot directly transmit or receive data across all transmitter and receiver pairs. Instead, each subcarrier data stream from a source node must use relayed through a single AF (amplify-and-forward) relay selected specifically for that link. The objective is to maximize the system's minimum secure secrecy rate (SSR) by jointly optimizing secrecy-weighted transmit power distribution and the complex power amplification factors at the relays. This optimization occurs under constraints regarding total power, individual peak power limits, successful decoding thresholds at users, and the requirement that data be encoded with the most robust modulation type feasible. Due to the non-convex nature of the problem, an iterative solution is developed using successive convex approximation (SCA). Within this approach, the difficult non-convex decoding threshold constraints are reformulated as a series of linear approximations updated in each step until convergence. Assuming fixed power allocations during a step, the problem achieves an optimal solution via a bisection method and closed-form expressions. Furthermore, closed-form formulas for upper bounds of the achievable sum-rate and the worst-case SSR are derived to offer insights. Finally, numerical simulations are provided to validate the proposed model and its performance metrics.

Text-based games present a unique challenge in artificial general agent research, serving as a rich source for evaluating models' common-sense reasoning, natural language understanding, and theoretical progress, with benchmarks like StoryOfGames and GLUE highlighting models that have improved significantly over the past years. Nevertheless, existing game engines rely on resource-heavy Python implementations, creating severe execution bottlenecks that strictly limit operational speed to approximately 1,000 actions per second; this performance barrier forces Generative Adapters, even optimized ones, to spend nearly an hour adapting to a single level. To resolve this, we introduce TextWorldExpress, a complete, modern C++ reconstruction of the TextWorld platform featuring full compatibility with Generative Adapters and past improvements, delivering massive velocity boosts including a 500-fold increase over the original Python version. We push the platform further by introducing parallel execution capabilities, enabling it to surpass one million actions per second in markovian environments such as our developed MAPMA (Markov Adapters for Parallel Multi-Agent Play Adapters).

Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, despite their effectiveness in image recognition and natural language processing, face significant challenges when used for video analysis due to excessive computational costs and low energy efficiency. Addressing this, we introduce an innovative hardware and algorithm co-design approach. The methodology begins with Hardware-Algo Co-Tuning (HAT), which optimizes network architecture by applying pruning, channel reordering, and quantization to achieve a balance between high accuracy and efficiency. Subsequently, the process employs Hierarchical Tucker Tensor Decomposition (HTTD) to create an efficient video recognizer. HTTD models video data by treating a sequence of flattened frames as a three-dimensional tensor, learning an efficient representation where spatial and temporal hierarchies are computed independently to minimize processing loads. Experimental results on standard video benchmarks confirm that this two-phase method significantly lowers both the energy usage and complexity of building real-world visual systems based on LSTM.

Hypathese testing serves as a core and well-established element of the statistical inference process, frequently relying on the Bayes factor to evaluate competing hypotheses regarding a data-generating process. This approach explicitly integrates prior information and allows for the rejection of statistical hypotheses, with the associated "Bayes factor" quantifying the relative support in data for one hypothesis against another. By defining a set of properties for functions tasked with capturing key aspects of this subsegments and constructing hierarchical items based on these functions, we present extended "workflows" designed to elucidate competitive nested models utilizing Bayes factors. Testing this method on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrates its efficacy in offering intuitive, robust assessments of nested model systems.

This work challenges the assumption that nonconvex two-parameter matrix decomposition problems are inherently complex by demonstrating that specific nonconvex decomposable optimization problems, although nonconvex in their original parameters, become strictly geodesically convex when parametrized with fixed, rank. This rank-parametrization transforms the search space into a smooth Riemannian manifold, enabling strict convexity along geodesics within well-defined neighborhoods of the global minimum. Consequently, these problems possess a simple global geometry that guarantees convergence to a unique global optimum from any starting point. We provide sufficient conditions for this geodesic convexity and illustrate how strictly decomposable problems fit this framework, a property that subsumes many previously studied nonconvex scenarios. By establishing that such difficulties vanish under fixed-rank transformation, our findings offer a fresh, rigorous re-examination of global geometry analysis in matrix optimization from the perspective of Riemannian methods.

A combinatorial edge coloring of a graph $G$ involves assigning colors to its edges such that no two adjacent edges share the same color. Let $\Delta(G)$ represent the maximum degree found among all vertices in $G$. A coloring scheme is classified as robust if, for any specific color, removing all edges of that color from $G$ results in a forest (which contains no cycles). It is an established fact that a robust coloring exists using at most $\Delta(G)+1$ colors whenever $\Delta(G)$ is at least 3. However, in this paper, we demonstrate through a counterexample that a cubic bipartite graph for which 4 colors are sufficient for a robust coloring does not currently have its deterministic algorithm determined, specifically highlighting the necessity of four colors given the graph's triangle-free structure (lacking both triangles and quadrangles).

We examine a version of a Cournot market distinction involving multiple participants where every individual acts according to their own self-learning process. In this context, self-learning is process refers to individually adaptive processes. In this context, self-learning refers to the process of individual adaptability. Specifically, each participant's adaptability process involves adjusting two key parameters: first, the quantity supplied to the market and, second, the rule used to estimate other participants' adaptability processes. The study focuses on a scenario where a limited number of self-learning individuals interact within the market. Using two self-adaptive self-learning approaches, we investigate the short-term dynamics of this specific learning scenario. Our analysis reveals that in this short-term dynamic, both learning approaches favor a state in which participants' adaptability processes converge to a Nash equilibrium. This result implies a more general statement regarding the equality of Humpbackelr's and other similar operators applied to these ideals. As an additional contribution, we establish equality between the symbolic and typical powers for the specified class of oriented bipartite graphs $\mathcal{D}$. Furthermore, we determine the explicit formula for typical algebraic rank of the power $I(\mathcal{D})^a$ when applied to non-oriented bipartite graphs, and provide the complete formula for their symbolic powers.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical systems, yet their susceptibility to adversarial attacks remains a major concern. This paper proposes using the histogram of activation values as a mechanism to anticipate and mitigate such risks. We demonstrate that legitimate and adversarially perturbed inputs produce distinctly different ranges of activation value distributions, with our findings suggesting this gap offers a transferable defense strategy across various CNN models. We introduce a novel architecture named Range Supervision (RS) that leverages these ranges to defend against black-box and white-box adversarial examples. Extensive testing on ImageNet and natural dataset assessments confirms that our approach matches state-of-the-art transferable defense methods in preserving model accuracy and effectively neutralizing adversarial attacks. Additionally, we provide a rigorous safety case, grounded in the Argument-driven Root-cause Analysis (Adora) framework, supporting the hypothesis that range-based transferable defense enhances convolutional network robustness against attacks.

We provide an explicit construction of a continuous parameter family of Jordanian twists associated with the twisted affine Kac-Moody Lie algebras $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(2)$ through $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(6)$. For these collections, the differential operator governing the classical r-functionals coincides precisely with that defining the classical Liouville r-functional. Furthermore, we conjecture that all such parameters are indeed continuous. Finally, within the specific case of $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}_2}^{\wedge}$ within the dual of the twice-twisted affine Kac-Moody algebra, we demonstrate that the classical Liouville case is the only unique persistent classical integrable configuration across all classical integrable models derived from quasi-Shapovalov modules.

We propose a method for multi-lingual word representations that preserves semantic consistency across languages, addressing the critical challenge of aligning semantic areas from different language embedding spaces. Although these spaces often exhibit near-linear manifold structures, we address their inconsistent metrices. We project embeddings from all languages into a common semanticare without requiring pre-trained multilingual representations or cross-lingual mappings, ensuring effective multi-lingual representation. Specifically, we assume a cluster-consistent relationship between the original embedding areas and our target common space to ensure structure preservation. We propose cluster-kmeans-based algorithms for both individual and concurrent representations, along with an optimization framework to guide projection without assuming the target space's specific distribution. Loss functions are designed to enforce cluster consistency, achieve clustering in the new area, and bind each cluster to a representative anchor. The resulting multi-lingual area supports diverse applications, particularly cross-lingual tasks benefiting aggregated multi-lingual clustering.

In the spring of 2019, millions of Chileans took to the streets in a massive wave of protests, a movement fueled by widespread anger toward the socioeconomic system and a long-standing transport fare policy. These disturbances were so profound that they forced the new Chilean government to adopt non-uniform (non-local) urban mobility measures aimed at cutting urban traffic by half. The current study employs an epidemiological non-local mathematical framework to simulate the Chilean unrest. This model captures the influence of media coverage on the spread and intensity of the protests. The research involves formulating the problem within a rigorous mathematical framework, proving the existence and uniqueness of solutions, and conducting detailed asymptotic analysis with respect to the total population decay rate. Numerical simulations based on data that fills gaps where official records were unavailable reveal how the rate of population decline significantly influences both the duration and peak intensity of the social movement. Finally, by comparing model outputs with actual historical events, we validate the effectiveness of the proposed non-uniform (non-local) modeling approach.

This paper introduces a solution method for extended regular expression inequalities of the form $L(A) \leqslant L(B)$, where $A$ and $B$ are "regexes" adhering to syntax that allows term-wise application of functions such as $\log_2$, $\sin$, and others. The core definition of these functions is through specific graphs known as Reutenauer series; consequently, the resolution of such inequality problems reduces to a system of differential regex constraints. We demonstrate a solving algorithm for this class of differential regex inequalities by adapting the subset construction process to differential regexes, defining the derivative of these structures accordingly.

Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) has emerged as a leading technology for precise and real-time pose estimation across various industries, with deep learning-based methods currently attracting significant research interest. However, utilizing this approach for localization presents difficulties, as traditional image features often yield suboptimal performance, while generic deep models face challenges in simultaneously learning robust representation and accurate metering. In response, we present an external memory-based Very-light Integrated Odometer (EMA-VIO) designed to achieve robust representation learning and metering by leveraging cross-temporal feedback. Cross-temporal feedback helps correct errors and stabilize the system over time. Specifically, we utilize pose graphs and traditional VIO solutions to generate feedback that addresses errors in both geometric and metric domains, which is then organized into an external memory. This stored information guides the system through a dual-stream deep network architecture, facilitating very-light integrated operations. Extensive testing in both real-world and simulated environments demonstrates that EMA-VIO surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques, with live evaluations confirming its practical viability.

Square-root Weyl materials are a recent class of materials featuring multiple bands with nearly linear crossings, characterized by non-trivial Berry curvature and higher-order topological invariants. These features make them an attractive topic for both fundamental research and technological applications. In this paper, I introduce a new category of horizontal crossings defined by quadratic dispersion relations rooted in higher-order terms, designated as square-root HoWels. These quadratically disperse crossings exhibit unique geometric and topological attributes, including higher-order invariants that can be arbitrarily large, Hamiltonians belonging to distinct equivalence classes under unitary and anti-unitual transformations despite having the same higher-order kagome lattices, and massless Dirac fermions with helicity. Because the group velocity varies with direction, it can approach zero arbitrarily close to the touchings, potentially leading to ultra-low carrier mobility. Additionally, the strong dependence of the Bernou curvature and massless ferromagnetic moments on momentum can couple to other degrees of freedom, enabling the control through the higher-ord kagome magnetic fields. I propose that the lattice structure exists in the crystal and calculate the mathematical formulation, identifying the potential experimental signatures and the expected results.

This study presents numerical results derived from a quasi-reversibility approach applied to a data completion problem for Maxwell's equations. Specifically, the method determines both a missing portion of the refractive index and an initial electric field within a lossy domain, given only partial information about these fields at the boundary. Our analysis examines the a priori version of the problem by formulating it as a nonlinear variational issue, proving the uniqueness of the solution and establishing its convergence rates within specific Sobolev spaces. Furthermore, the paper introduces and analyzes a semi-discrete version using finite element methods. Spatio-temporal discretization details are omitted as they follow standard procedures. Our estimates of the method's convergence incorporate the impact of both incomplete data and numerical approximation errors, which together define the total perturbation. To validate the approach, several numerical experiments demonstrate its effectiveness in practice.

Superconducting quantum circuits are recognized as a foremost platform for quantum computing, yet realizing large-scale systems requires detecting and correcting material flaws at terahertz frequencies. Although transfer matrix theory is commonly applied to model microwave resonators and two-sided coupled transmission lines (TM), these approaches fail when applied to one-sided resonator configurations. This research utilizes near-field terahertz scanning microscopy to investigate the electric field distributions of terahertz surface waves (SWs) resonating on superconducting niobium meander-line structures. Following a quantitative analysis, these results are compared against standard transfer matrix models of lossy transmission line resonators. The study introduces an enhanced "one-sided" formalism, demonstrating superior agreement with empirical data by accurately capturing SW coupling and Terahertz-specific material losses. Furthermore, the findings highlight that traditional models, which do not account for unilateral geometric constraints, substantially underestimate intrinsic material losses in the terahertz spectrum.

This manuscript serves as a non-official translation of the Working Group 5.1 report (Atmospheric Evolution Feedbacks) for the IAU/VGP Symposium: Exploring the Past, Present, and Future of the Martian Atmosphere, held in Moscow in 2022, which was not published elsewhere due to its inclusion in private collections. It examines Venus's atmospheric history, emphasizing how key processes interact to regulate climate stability and assess the plausibility of atmospheric longevity using formal feedback mechanisms, particularly exploring the causes of historical continental-scale drying events.

This study introduces a Bayesian framework for estimating and forecasting various forms of multivariate Hawkes processes operating in nonlinear regimes. We evaluate the model's predictions using simulated data and real-world internet traffic datasets. Realizations from the posterior distributions highlight the approach's inherent flexibility and predictive capabilities when dealing with complex nonlinear dynamics. Additionally, we examine specific Bayesian estimators derived for this purpose that incorporate sparsity constraints and features induced through kernel methods.

High-intensity laser pulses facing magnetic fields constitute a formidable tool for exploring nonlinear interactions in plasma while simultaneously pushing the performance limits of laser technology. We demonstrate, both through Particle-in-Cell simulations and analytical modeling, that simultaneous self-amplification and conversion of linear polarization to circular polarization occur when multi-petawatt pulses navigate magnetized plasmas. This phenomenon stems from a coupling between electromagnetic amplification and the rotation of the polarization plane. Our findings provide a foundational framework for future experiments aiming to investigate these dynamics and generate more powerful, circularly polarized photons.

Constraints from BaBar and CERN/BNL EDM experiments yield a separate bound of $r_a < 0.6 \, \text{GeV}$. The upcoming Super $\tau$ factory is projected to enhance the single-EDM (EDM) quantity limit by an order of magnitude.

This section explores decoding techniques for Rank Metric Code (RMC) decoding tasks, specifically concentrating on a subset known as "symmetric" RMC where error matrices adhere to a constraint of non-negative and equal diagonal elements. The primary goal is to determine the feasibility of decoding these symmetric instances that suffer from a total key rate exceeding what asymmetric or zero-diagonal-restricted variants can manage. To achieve this, a novel decoder is established by integrating an information-theoretic approach with a geometric framework. The section further introduces a tight bound on the geometric rate of this code and supports all findings with extensive simulations that demonstrate the decoder's efficacy in practice.

We revisit the long-OPE blocks involving two spinning fields within two-dimensional conformal field theory. Furthermore, we examine their classical limit and explore the relationship between these OPE blocks and spinning geodesics defined in AdS$_{3}$ space, thereby enriching our understanding of the geometric underpinnings of quantum correlations in the AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ duality framework.

A primary obstacle to building reliable probabilities for dark matter halo masses remains the difficulty in accurately modeling their distribution across varied scenarios. Although numerous deep learning models have been developed to estimate these mass functions, they typically rely on simplified dark matter theories, such as $\Lambda$CDM, and often use approximated numerical methods for halo mass estimation. In this study, we present the first application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to calculate halo mass functions grounded in a "cosmic speed" dark matter framework. This specific theory aligns more closely with observed halo characteristics than the standard $\Lambda$CDM model. Our findings reveal that incorporating prior knowledge of halo scaling relations into the training process significantly enhances the accuracy of estimating halo mass functions under the cosmic speed dark matter assumption. Rich entity extraction for documents, such as detecting entities like names within emails, requires understanding the email's layout and design elements. Although existing approaches leverage visual characteristics to achieve high accuracy and F1 scores, these models depend on full-color labeled dataset images that are expensive to produce. Consequently, this study introduces "SketchDatalab," an online platform facilitating data labeling with only black-lines line drawings. Evaluations using three distinct labeling tasks—labeling tables, footnotes, and navigation—demonstrate that our platform reduces labeling costs by up to 93%, 91%, and 89%, respectively, while maintaining negligible impacts on model performance. Furthermore, the implementation details for replicating our system are provided within the paper.

Similarly, we obtain the Dysthe equation as a second fourth-order asymptotic model for the same system, but both differ from the standard Dysthe and Peterburgskii equations in their treatment of wave amplitude sign symmetry. We establish the local existence and uniqueness of solutions for these equations, observing that solution blow-up cannot occur within a time frame determined solely by the initial data magnitude. Furthermore, we prove that solutions to the Hamiltonian Dysthe equation asymptotically converge to those of the classical Dysthe equation, with the rate of convergence dependent exclusively on the initial data's spatial distribution characteristics.
